## Summary

The quarter review links software repricing to private-equity and credit risk, criticizes smoothed private valuations, and separates attractive new lending from legacy exposures. Eisman retains Meritage with a specific year-end buyback expectation and an explicit interest-rate caveat. He expects software incumbents to survive but lose seat and pricing momentum. His universal claim that every 2018-2022 PE software deal is underwater lacks transaction-level support; announced layoffs do not independently establish AI unemployment.

Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

## Framework and tools

- Smooth marks do not erase economic volatility.
- Separate new lending terms from old-fund recoveries.
- Use index weights to understand contribution without confusing stock values and GDP.
- Separate software survival from pricing power.
- Consider incentives and the timing of credit deterioration.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Q1 returns across eleven S&P sectors.
- Ten-year yield and oil-price changes.
- Private-fund redemption requests and caps.
- Medicare Advantage payment revision.
- Meritage tangible book and buyback target.
